headline: Adaptive feedback and modularity in computational models of neural and metabolic systems
label: Homeostatic And Adaptive Computational Models
summary: Models now embed adaptive regulation and learnable dynamics to test how neural and metabolic systems adapt to perturbation and temporal tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is embedding adaptive control in mechanistic computational models of neural and metabolic systems. A cerebellar-inspired feedforward module added to an RNN learns temporal tasks faster than parameter-matched recurrent baselines, and leaky-integrator RNNs with learnable time constants are dissected for multiple mechanisms of rhythm switching. In a whole-brain neural mass model, inhibitory synaptic plasticity clamps firing rates while the model is fit to EEG and fMRI. An ODE model of mammalian energy metabolism uses adaptive enzyme capacity and ATP-costed regulation to test whether prior perturbations improve later responses. A separate framework couples biological neural cultures to a simulated task through encoding and decoding parameter optimization. What is new is the explicit use of adaptive parameters, whether time constants, enzyme levels, or synaptic rules, as the substrate of the computation, with validation against task performance or empirical recordings. The shared element is architectural and dynamical rather than data-type specific.
